ProgramName: Master of Architecture
Description:
Architecture is a highly synthetic discipline that requires a complex mix of cultural awareness, technical expertise, and creative facility. This is architecture's great draw, and its great challenge. How do we engage a world that is marked by diverse people, ever-changing digital technologies and dynamic ecologies?  
The a program at the Knowlton School is dedicated to all aspects of this pursuit and is grounded in an understanding of architecture as a cultural enterprise. We are invested in the knowledge of architecture's traditions through strengths in history and theory while we transform the discipline through technology and engagement with the world. Seminars in history and theory are supplemented by courses in systems, sustainability, structures and professional practice, reinforced by the school's extensive fabrication and computing facilities.  
Most importantly, cultural breadth and technical depth are synthesized in the school's intensive studio culture where students creatively engage real world issues. In addition, the program offers opportunities for internships and international travel and is able to provide more than half of our students with ﬁnancial support.  
The Master of Architecture degree at the Knowlton School has a single degree structure with a three-year sequence and two entry points. Students with non-architecture undergraduate degrees, and some continuing students, enter in the first year, which focuses on the development of the student's critical, technical and aesthetic sensibility within the domain of architectural design. Students who have completed a four-year undergraduate degree from an NAAB-accredited program may be granted advanced placement to enter the second year on the basis of academic performance and portfolio review.
Accredidation: Fully accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board (NAAB). [1]

About us

The pri­ma­ry mis­sion of our grad­u­ate pro­gram is to edu­cate stu­dents as research econ­o­mists. As they pur­sue PhD degrees, our grad­u­ate stu­dents acquire a wide range of skills that make them excel­lent uni­ver­si­ty teach­ers and pro­fes­sion­al econ­o­mists. An advanced degree in eco­nom­ics offers an excit­ing range of career choice in acad­e­mia, busi­ness and government.

About 80 grad­u­ate stu­dents are in the eco­nom­ics PhD pro­gram. Our enter­ing class con­sists of approx­i­mate­ly 15–20 stu­dents select­ed from a very com­pet­i­tive pool of approx­i­mate­ly 300 appli­cants from all over the world. In recent years, we have ranked in the top eche­lon of all depart­ments at The Ohio State Uni­ver­si­ty in the num­ber of uni­ver­si­ty fel­low­ships award­ed to new grad­u­ate stu­dents. We also pro­vide con­fer­ence trav­el sup­port, dis­ser­ta­tion research sup­port and sup­port for the job mar­ket prepa­ra­tions of our dis­ser­ta­tion students.

The fac­ul­ty and department

The ded­i­ca­tion of our grad­u­ate fac­ul­ty to excel­lence in eco­nom­ics edu­ca­tion is reflect­ed in the depth and breadth of their research activ­i­ties. Our fac­ul­ty includes three Fel­lows of the Econo­met­ric Soci­ety and sev­er­al edi­tors and asso­ciate edi­tors of top-ranked eco­nom­ics jour­nals. We are in the Top 10 ranked eco­nom­ics pro­grams among pub­lic uni­ver­si­ties and in the top 25 of all U.S. eco­nom­ics depart­ments in terms of pub­li­ca­tion productivity.

Op­tion­al Prac­ti­cal Train­ing (OPT)

In­ter­na­tion­al grad­u­ates of this major are eli­gi­ble per the Depart­ment of Home­land Secu­ri­ty to apply for up to three (3) years of work per­mis­sion in the Unit­ed States after grad­u­a­tion. See the Office of Inter­na­tion­al Affairs web­site for more eli­gi­bil­i­ty require­ments.

[11]

At both levels, an emphasis is placed on two of the requirements for present day geographers - theoretical understanding and methodological skills. Within the profession, the department is known for its theoretical and empirical approaches in four specialty areas: Environment and Society, Atmospheric and Climatic Studies, GIS and Spatial Analysis, and Urban, Regional and Global Studies. [12] The Master's program in Geography is typically a two year program. During that time, you will complete a small series of core courses and work closely with your faculty advisor to develop a curriculum that best suits your research interests. The program is designed to have you demonstrate that you are capable of identifying a research problem as well as marshalling the conceptual and methodological tools to address it. [15]

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Global One Health
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree or an advanced degree that includes foundational courses in college-level math, biology, and chemistry. A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 is also a prerequisite. [1, 2] Applicants can be current graduate or professional degree-seeking students or working professionals. [2] The program requires the completion of 15 graduate credit hours. [1]

Description: The Graduate Certificate in Global One Health is designed for both current graduate/professional students and working professionals who already hold a graduate or professional degree. [1] The program's purpose is to add One Health courses and content to augment their curriculum or enhance their specialized expertise. [2] There is a recognized need for an interdisciplinary and integrated One Health approach to address surveillance, prevention, and intervention for agents and diseases at the intersection of human, animal, and environmental health. [1] With a Global One Health graduate certificate, students will learn about the inextricable links among human health, animal health, and environmental health to make a holistic impact in disease prevention and mitigation. [3] This is a 15-credit program offering both online and in-person learning for a deeper understanding of epidemiology, environmental health sciences, and zoonotic diseases. [3] Upon completion, individuals will be better prepared to address complex interdisciplinary issues, interpret monitoring and surveillance data, summarize major categories of infectious microbial pathogens and other hazardous agents, and describe the dynamics of disease determinants. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Greek and Latin
Requirements: Applicants for the Ph.D. in Greek and Latin should be proficient in at least one and preferably both languages. A knowledge of French and/or German and some preparation in ancillary disciplines such as history, philosophy, linguistics, religious studies, or art and archaeology are also desirable. [7] The application checklist includes: Apply online with the nonrefundable application fee (US$60 for domestic applicants, US$70 for international applicants); a statement of intent; an academic CV; a list of works the applicant has read in the original Greek or Latin; a writing sample; and scans of official transcripts. [7]
Description: The graduate program in the Department of Classics at Ohio State provides students with a solid foundation for careers in research and teaching at the university or college level, as well as for careers in secondary school teaching. The program is designed to familiarize students with the languages, literature, and culture of ancient Greece and Rome, and to introduce them to the methods and techniques of modern classical scholarship. The program offers M.A. and Ph.D. degrees, and is administered by the departmental Graduate Studies Committee. The Department of Classics also participates in a number of interdepartmental programs, such as the Center for Epigraphical and Palaeographical Studies, the Interdisciplinary Ph.D. Program in the History of Art, the Interdisciplinary Program in Ancient History, the Center for Medieval and Renaissance Studies, and the new graduate program in Religious Studies. Students interested in these programs should consult the appropriate sections of this handbook and the Graduate School Bulletin.

Applicants for the Ph.D. in Modern Greek should be proficient in Modern Greek. A knowledge of French and/or German and some preparation in ancillary disciplines such as history, philosophy, linguistics, religious studies, or art and archaeology are also desirable. [5]
Description: The Ph.D. degree in Greek and Latin is awarded upon successful completion of a program of study in the Latin and Greek languages, literatures, and related subjects. The requirements of the program include courses, language examinations (ancient and modern), the candidacy examination, and the dissertation. [2]

Requirements: To be admitted to the HRS PhD program, each applicant must fulfill the following criteria: Graduate Program Application; Overall 3.0+ GPA (and TOEFL if applicable); Official Transcripts; Hold a Professional or Master's degree (or equivalent) at the time of matriculation; Identification of a PhD Advisor – Each applicant must submit a prospective advisor agreement form and indicate a clear commitment from a P-status graduate faculty member from HRS. Description: TThe PhD in Health and Rehabilitation Sciences at The Ohio State University aims to train independent scientific researchers who will make meaningful contributions to their field in research-focused careers in academia, government, or industry. [5] The HRS PhD Program has a mission to develop transformative leaders at the forefront of scientific discovery with a vision to be a global leader in advancing scholarship and leadership by developing excellent interdisciplinary scientists. [5] HRS PhD students will become stewards of their science by applying rigorous and ethical scientific methods, and cutting-edge analytical approaches in a focused domain of science that aligns with their professional goals. [5] Our graduates will lead their disciplines by engaging in life-long research. [5]

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Health and Wellness Coaching
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Health and Wellness Coaching provides an overview of the health and wellness coach role, theory, and competencies with application to coaching skills. It focuses on the theory and application of evidence-based coaching approaches for lifestyle behavior change as integrated within interprofessional practice. The program includes critical analysis of theoretical and research findings in motivational interviewing to create behavior change and improve health outcomes. It builds upon an introductory coaching course to refine skills that promote whole-person health. [4] This enhanced approach supports holistic health promotion and lifestyle behavior change, emphasizing the nine dimensions of wellness: emotional, career, social, intellectual, spiritual, physical, financial, creative, and environmental. [4] The certificate is open to students with a bachelor's degree in a health-related field and prepares them to use coaching strategies in various healthcare settings. [4]

The 100% online Master of Healthcare Innovation at The Ohio State University is open to applicants with any undergraduate degree. This radically different approach offers a streamlined path to the development of healthcare leaders while integrating personal wellness with the principles of innovation and change. The MHI answers the important need for healthcare leaders who understand complex dynamics, are prepared to apply revolutionary ideas and create new models of care.

The first two years are devoted to intensive coursework and to the fulfillment of the writing requirements for the MA degree (either a thesis or two qualifying papers). The MGEL is designed to provide maximum flexibility for busy, working, professional engineers. Description: The online Master of Supply Chain Management (MSCM) degree at The Ohio State University Max M. [3] The MSCM builds and refines valuable supply chain skills through a flexible curriculum that combines online coursework with hands-on learning experiences. [3] Graduates will represent a new generation of supply chain professionals equipped to immediately put the latest theory into practice. The program offers part-time or full-time options, with content delivered 50% live and 50% self-paced, and includes on-campus immersion experiences and a hands-on, signature capstone project. [3]

Description: The Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering at The Ohio State University is designed for students with a bachelor's degree in a science or engineering discipline. It implies the mathematical maturity and ability requisite of a faculty member at the university level, and one who is expected to advance the discipline of mathematics through research and teaching. We seek to achieve this through thorough training in the core areas in mathematics, research specialization and teaching of undergraduate mathematics. Graduates will have demonstrated their ability to conduct independent scientific research and contribute new mathematical knowledge and scholarship in their area of specialization. They will be well-supported and well prepared for research and faculty positions at academic institutions anywhere in the world. Owing to their independence, analytic abilities, and proven tenacity, our PhD graduates are also sought after by private and government employers. Our PhD program offers two tracks, one for Theoretical Mathematics and one for Applied Mathematics. The tracks differ only in the course and qualifying requirements during the first two years.

The master's aprogram is an ideal fit for professionals in the fields of medicine, nursing, dentistry, social work, veterinary medicine, genetic counseling, public policy, and biotechnology as well as science researchers. [2] The accredited MCR program prepares students to excel as administrators, regulatory specialists and other professional roles on clinical research teams. [2] The program offers a multidisciplinary curriculum, covering the theory and practice of research methods and statistics, the ethics of human subjects research, the science of pharmacology and medical product regulation, and the business of research operations and management. [2] This program is open to applicants with any undergraduate degree. [2] The program concludes with a culminating project where students have an opportunity to apply best practices in clinical research operations or administration. [2]

[1] Program goals: Prepare graduates for faculty and administrative positions in dental hygiene programs. Provide graduates with an appreciation of the skills necessary to be leaders in the profession. Prepare graduates to contribute to the body of knowledge in dental hygiene through research and scholarly activity. The graduate program consists of courses in education, research, leadership, including a thesis and an internship. Description: Building on a strong history of innovation in nutrition and dietetics education, research and community outreach, The Ohio State University offers the Master of Dietetics and Nutrition (MDN). [3] The MDN is a clinical, two-year accredited program that provides the didactic education, as well as the supervised practice experiences, to meet the competency-based education approach under the Future Education Model to prepare students to practice as an entry-level registered dietitian nutritionist. [3, 4] The program is designed for students who have a bachelor's degree in any major and would like to pursue a registered dietitian graduate program. [4] It is administered as a collaboration of the Department of Human Sciences in the College of Education and Human Ecology with the School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences in the College of Medicine. The curriculum is structured to provide students with an advanced understanding of the chemical, physical, and biological properties of food. Research is a significant component of the program, with students having the opportunity to work with faculty on a wide range of research topics. These research areas are dedicated to solving real problems within the food system, from harvest and processing to consumption and individual health. Students are invited to work alongside faculty on research projects in areas such as food allergens, bioinformatics, biotechnology, food chemistry, food engineering, human health, food microbiology, food processing, food safety, and risk analysis. Logistics management is the act of supervising the movement of goods to the right place at the right time. A typical logistics system includes customer service, demand forecasting, distribution, communications, inventory control, material handling, order processing, parts and service support, location analysis, purchasing, packaging, return goods handling, salvage and scrap disposal, traffic and transportation, and warehousing and storage. Jobs in small companies may involve all of these, while positions at large corporations may focus on only one or a few of these areas.
Accredidation: The Ohio State University Max M. Fisher College of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Marketing

Admission to the university is competitive. There are no specific prerequisite courses required for admission to the pre-major program. However, students are expected to complete a rigorous college preparatory curriculum.
Concentration: In addition to required marketing course work, students have the opportunity to select a track of courses from the areas of research analyst, sales client management, communications or product development. [10]

The study of marketing includes the process of planning and implementing the conception, pricing, promotion and delivery of the ideas, goods and services involved in these exchanges. [10]
Accredidation: The Ohio State University Max M. ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Operations Management
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Operations Management is granted upon admission to the Columbus campus. The Ohio State University uses a holistic review process that considers several factors. These include the successful completion of Ohio State's minimum college preparatory curriculum, high school performance (including class rank or GPA and participation in accelerated programs like AP or IB), and standardized test scores (ACT or SAT). [6] The university also evaluates experiences that show leadership or engaged involvement, such as co-curricular activities and work experience. [6]
Concentration: ['Operations', 'Purchasing']
Description: Operations management is the systematic direction and control of the processes that transform inputs into finished goods and services. The operations function comprises a significant percentage of the employees and physical assets in most organizations. Operations managers are concerned with each step in providing a service or product. They determine what equipment, labor, tools, facilities, materials, energy and information should go into an operating system and how these inputs can best be obtained and used to satisfy the requirements of the market place. Managers are also responsible for critical activities such as quality management and control, capacity planning, materials management, purchasing and scheduling.
Accredidation: The Ohio State University's Fisher College of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). [2, 5] This accreditation is a voluntary, nongovernmental process that includes a rigorous external review of a school's mission, faculty qualifications, curricula, and ability to provide high-quality programs. [2] Fisher College of Business is one of the founding members of the AACSB. [3] In 2024, the AACSB renewed the college's accreditation for another five years. [2]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, and for specific programs like study abroad.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in Real Estate and Urban Analysis

Many areas of the financial services industry—loan origination and servicing, portfolio investment and advising—require extensive real estate knowledge. As students progress in their real estate careers, they typically acquire designations from and participate in one or more professional associations.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering

Description: Chemical engineering students study changes in the composition, energy content or state of aggregation of materials and take into consideration the fundamentals of the nature of matter and its properties (chemistry); the forces that act on matter (physics); and the relationships between them (mathematics). Chemical engineering differs from chemistry in its emphasis on commercial applications of chemical reactions and separations and techniques for designing, operating and controlling processes. [5] The chemical engineering program in the William G. Lowrie Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering educates engineers to design, develop and operate chemical processes by which chemicals, petroleum products, food, pharmaceuticals and consumer goods can be produced economically and safely. [5] Products and processes must be environmentally friendly and safe. Chemical engineering processes usually involve chemical reactions and separations to produce more useful and valuable products. [5]

Description: The BS degree in chemistry requires 42 credit hours beyond general chemistry in the major program; 14–17 hours in calculus, analytic geometry and differential equations; and 10 hours in physics. [20] All human activities deal with a material world, which consists of chemicals both natural and manufactured. The contributions of chemistry to modern society occur in diverse fields, such as pharmaceuticals, polymers, agricultural chemicals, petroleum products and biotechnology. [20] Chemistry also plays a role in cleaning up the environment; improving methods of producing, processing and packaging food; and making automobiles safer and more fuel-efficient. [20]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chinese
Requirements: Upon admission to the university, students can declare a major in Chinese within the College of Arts and Sciences. Description: The Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures offers an undergraduate major in Chinese. The major program includes studies in language, literature and linguistics. [4] In addition to five levels of Chinese (Mandarin) language, two semesters of Classical Chinese, and the possibility of a combined BA/BS degree with the Chinese Flagship MA program, faculty teach a range of courses from introductions to Chinese culture, literature in translation, and linguistics to film and media. [4] The Chinese Language Program includes 5 levels of instruction in as many as 3 formats: Individualized Instruction, Intensive classroom, and Regular classroom (five hours per week). [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the College of Engineering is competitive. Applicants are first admitted to a pre-major program and must meet specific criteria to be placed into the Civil Engineering major.
Description: Civil engineers plan, design and build the structures and systems essential to American civilization: buildings, bridges, tunnels and dams; harbors and airports; waterways, railways and highways; water treatment plants; irrigation and drainage systems; landfills; and wastewater treatment plants. [13] Civil engineering at Ohio State offers the prospective student an exciting academic program enhanced by experiences in state-of-the-art laboratory facilities. [13] We offer a challenging environment designed to provide students with the resources and background necessary to pursue activities in the many different areas of civil engineering. [13] The department's professors are internationally recognized as leaders in their respective areas. [13]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering (BSCE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET. [14, 18]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Departmental, and External scholarships.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication
Requirements: Admission to the communication major is a competitive process that happens after a student has been admitted to The Ohio State University. Students interested in the major typically start as pre-majors and must complete two pre-major courses, COMM 1100 and COMM 1101, with a grade of C- or better. Application to the major is then based on cumulative grade point average, the completion of these pre-major courses, and enrollment capacity. The application itself is a brief online form.

Description: There is no greater tool in the world than successful communication in all forms—written, spoken and conceptual—and The Ohio State University's School of Communication provides students with the training and skill to harness the power of communication. Our program equips students with the practical and analytical skills and knowledge related to communication principles--how to understand audiences, shape messages and interact with individuals and technologies, as well as the power and influence of communication on society.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Engineering major, freshmen applying to the Columbus campus are strongly encouraged to submit their complete admission application by November 1. [1] Admitted first-year students begin in pre-computer science and engineering and complete the prerequisite course work necessary to apply to the major. [1]

Description: Computer science and engineering (CSE) focuses on the development of software and the uses of software to solve practical problems and to support and improve productivity, health, happiness and safety in today's society. Topics studied include algorithms and data structures, programming languages, computer architecture, computer graphics, operating systems, software engineering systems analysis, database systems, artificial intelligence, information security, and networking. CSE combines the technical study of both software and hardware.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Dance
Requirements: Acceptance into the BFA in Dance program requires an application to The Ohio State University Undergraduate Admissions (Columbus campus) AND the Department of Dance Audition. The Admission Common Application will open in August; the Dance Audition application will open in mid-June. We encourage all auditionees to prepare and submit BOTH applications simultaneously, though the two decisions operate on independent timelines and processes that coordinate efforts. We do not pre-screen auditionees, but the audition application deadlines are firm. While it is not required, we strongly recommend that Dance applicants submit a letter of recommendation from a core academic subject high school teacher or counselor that will specifically address any insights into your academic context (not dance). Acceptance into the BFA Program is determined through careful consideration of your: dance training, experience, and goals, essay for Ohio State Admissions, activities and interests outside of dance, required creative prompt (solo) and interview responses.
Description: An accredited member of the National Association of Schools of Dance, the Department of Dance offers students rigorous training at the intersection of movement practice, creative activity and theoretical inquiry. [4] Students in the dance program earn a Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) and receive a comprehensive education across the field of contemporary dance with a focus on the dancing experience. [4] Because the BFA dance program is focused on building the whole artist, students can combine academic and artistic interests. [4] While dance is the focal point of their academic practice, students can choose from a variety of courses to enrich, extend and support their areas of investigation. [4] Students in the BFA dance program take course work in movement practice, performance, choreography, history/theory/literature, analysis, dance education, kinesiology, production and creative technology. [4] They benefit from small classes with faculty and visiting artists. [4] Faculty mentorship begins early and integrates with personalized education, individualized attention, and first- and last-year seminars that develop cohort community. [4] Upon completion of the foundational curriculum, students choose from a range of courses, such as Improvisation, Music and Choreography; Dance in Global Contexts; Dance Film; and Intermedia Performance. Accredidation: The Ohio State University is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD). [14, 15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Data Analytics
Requirements: Admission to the data analytics major is competitive. Factors considered include the cumulative GPA, the grades earned in a defined set of rigorous, foundational courses, and a statement of interest. Most successful applicants have a cumulative GPA of 3.2 or higher.
Concentration: ['Biomedical and public health analytics', 'Business analytics', 'Computational analytics', 'Data visualization', 'Social science analytics']
Description: Data analytics applies fundamental scientific principles to the analysis of large, complex data sets. This rapidly growing field needs practitioners with expertise that cuts across core disciplines of computer science, mathematics and statistics and with highly developed critical-thinking, problem-solving and communication skills. Data analytics includes the set of skills necessary to manage, represent and manipulate large, complex data stores; to abstract, model and effectively analyze such data; and to create quantitative visual cues to help explain and make informed decisions from those data.
ScholarshipAmount: Over $575,000 in scholarships have been awarded to 144 students within the Data Analytics major. [17]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Dental Hygiene
Description: This four year program includes basic sciences and general education courses followed by the professional training required to prepare students to practice dental hygiene. In addition to preparation for licensure in dental hygiene, the baccalaureate program prepares students for roles of leadership and responsibility in a variety of health care settings. A dental hygienist is a preventive oral health professional who is licensed in dental hygiene. A dental hygienist provides education, clinical, and therapeutic services supporting total health through the promotion of oral health.
Accredidation: The program in dental hygiene is accredited by the Commission on Dental Accreditation and has been granted the accreditation status of “approval without reporting requirements.” The Commission is a specialized accrediting body recognized by the United States Department of Education.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Design in Industrial Design

The review process is holistic and considers your academic record, rigor of your curriculum, your essay, and your involvement.

Description: The Industrial Design program at The Ohio State University empowers students to design objects, services, and systems that enhance everyday life. With a strong foundation in design thinking and research, students explore how to develop innovative solutions that address real human needs. [3] The curriculum integrates knowledge of manufacturing, systems analysis, and sustainability, encouraging students to think critically about how design can shape the future. [3] All Design students begin in the 18-credit hour collaborative Design Foundations program, a shared first-year experience where students build core creative, technical, and collaborative skills before applying to their chosen major. [3] The Bachelor of Science in Design (BSD) is a Professional Degree, meaning over 65% of the course credit is focused on the creation and study of art and design. [19] Its lock-step curriculum takes students through a specific sequence of studio-based courses, designed to scaffold skills and increase in scale, scope, complexity, and collaboration with each semester. [19]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Design in Interior Design
Description: The Interior Design program at The Ohio State University prepares students to design environments that enhance human experience and well-being. [10] With a strong emphasis on commercial, workplace, hospitality, educational, and healthcare spaces, students learn to apply design thinking and research to create functional, sustainable, and aesthetically compelling interiors. [10] The curriculum blends studio practice with technical and theoretical coursework, encouraging students to explore spatial design opportunities informed by environmental conditions and user needs. [10] Collaboration and sustainability are key pillars of the program, helping students develop holistic approaches to interior design. [10] Throughout their studies, students engage in real-world challenges and interdisciplinary projects, culminating in a final capstone that demonstrates their ability to work independently and lead in the field of environmental design. [10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Design in Visual Communication Design

Through a human-centered approach, students explore diverse areas such as brand identity, wayfinding, packaging, publication, web/mobile interfaces, and data visualization. Courses integrate advanced computing and digital media tools, enabling students to produce refined, professional-level work. The curriculum emphasizes design research, storytelling, and social relevance, preparing students to tackle complex communication challenges across industries. Students develop solutions that address key themes—education, health, culture, and social impact—and present their final projects in a public spring exhibition. This program fosters creativity, technical skill, and strategic thinking, empowering graduates to become leaders in the evolving field of visual communication.
Accredidation: All four visual arts units are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Early and Middle Childhood Education

Students may also elect to participate in the cooperative education program or the combined five-year BS/MS degree program.

They craft short stories, sonnets and creative non-fiction essays. They publish blog posts and produce videos. They write research papers, grant proposals and technical reports, and they organize social media campaigns. They become persuasive speakers, empathetic listeners, critical readers and sophisticated writers. Most importantly, they are prepared to thrive in fast-paced, ever-changing professional environments.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering

Requirements: For admission to the Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science program at the Columbus campus, applicants are considered on a competitive basis. These include the successful completion of Ohio State's minimum college preparatory requirements, high school performance (such as GPA or class rank), and participation in accelerated programs like AP, IB, or Honors. Ohio State does not set minimum requirements for GPA or class rank. [8] First-year applicants to the Columbus campus are required to apply through the Common Application and will need to complete Ohio State-specific questions within the application. These issues are at the forefront of the most pressing challenges facing the world. Students in this major take an array of science courses to foster understandings of the environment, its components and processes, and techniques for managing and restoring ecosystems within it. [21] Students completing this program earn the degree Bachelor of Science in Environment and Natural Resources. [11] Environmental Science allows students to investigate and seek out natural solutions to environmental problems, badge learning to preserve, restore, manage, and support both the living and nonliving components of our fragile ecosystems in order to ensure a healthy environment. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Exercise Science Education

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Fashion and Retail Studies

Our majors complete core courses in world cinema and the fundamental tools of film analysis; fulfill requirements in early cinema, multicultural film studies and the documentary and experimental traditions; and go on to take a series of elective courses, eventually designating a three course focus area for their studies. [4]
Accredidation: The Department of Theatre, Film, and Media Arts is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST). [16]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Food, Agricultural and Biological Engineering
Requirements: Applicants to The Ohio State University's Columbus campus are considered on a competitive basis through a holistic review process. [3]
Accredidation: The Agricultural Engineering, BSFABE, is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET. The Food, Biological, and Ecological Engineering, BSFABE, is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET. [3, 4]

[5] Each student is required to complete an internship to gain hands-on, practical experience in the food industry. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Food Science and Technology

Applicants are admitted to the university and can then declare their major. There are no additional application requirements specified for this program beyond the general university application.

[1] The food science and technology curriculum produces graduates who are well prepared to work in the public or private sector.
