Students develop their language proficiency—listening, speaking, reading and writing skills—in interactive classroom settings, in our individualized instruction program, and in study abroad settings in France, Canada and Senegal. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geography
Requirements: Application to The Ohio State University for undergraduate admission is conducted through a holistic review process. This includes consideration of the successful completion of the university's minimum college preparatory coursework, high school performance (GPA and class rank), and experiences that show leadership or engaged involvement. [4] For the 2026 admissions cycle and beyond, ACT or SAT scores are required for all new first-year undergraduate applicants to the Columbus campus. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in German
Requirements: First-year applicants to Ohio State's Columbus campus apply using the Common Application. This includes the submission of Ohio State-specific questions. A personal statement essay is a required part of the Common Application.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in German provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the German language, literature, and culture. The program aims to develop students' proficiency in reading, writing, speaking, and listening in German, while also providing a deep knowledge of the historical and cultural contexts of German-speaking countries. Students will engage with a variety of texts and media, from classical literature to contemporary film, and are encouraged to develop critical thinking and analytical skills. The major prepares students for a variety of careers in fields such as international relations, business, translation, and education, or for further graduate-level study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health and Rehabilitation Sciences
Requirements: To apply for admission to the professional program, students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.50 in all coursework from any accredited institution. [14] All prerequisite courses, including subjects like Anatomy, Human Physiology, Math, and various sciences, must be completed with a grade of C- or higher before starting the program. [14] Admission to the major is typically done through a secondary application process after a student is already enrolled at Ohio State as a pre-major. [3]
Department: School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences
Description: The health sciences program is a foundational undergraduate degree that introduces students to the health care field and provides in-depth science learning which prepares them for a health-related career or a graduate professional health program. [16] This unique undergraduate degree may be used by students to enter the workforce or to apply to a graduate professional program including medicine, dentistry, occupational therapy, physical therapy, public health, hospital administration, physician's assistant, nurse practitioner and medical dietetics. [16] The Health Sciences Program is offered by the School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences at The Ohio State University College of Medicine. [17] The program also offers the opportunity for students to complete their bachelor's degree after achieving an associate's degree in a related health care field. [17] Graduates are prepared for entry-level career opportunities in health care and health-related services or for entry into graduate and professional programs. [10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Information Management and Systems
Requirements: Admission to the Health Information Management and Systems (HIMS) professional program is a competitive process that occurs after a student has completed prerequisite coursework. The admission process is based on a holistic review of each candidate, which includes academic achievement in prerequisite courses and the student's overall cumulative grade-point average. A minimum GPA of 2.50 is required, though the average for entering classes is typically higher. All prerequisite courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. Competitive applicants will be invited for a personal interview to discuss their knowledge of the profession and career goals. It is also highly recommended that applicants interview or shadow a Health Information Management professional.
Department: School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences
Description: A dynamic field that bridges business management, information systems technology, and clinical science. With a solid business and information systems background, as well as a broad healthcare foundation, professionals lend their expertise in a variety of areas such as management, data analytics, quality improvement, legal and ethical issues, and research. Admitted first-year students begin in pre-health information management and systems. There they complete the prerequisite course work necessary to apply to the health information management and systems major. [5]
ScholarshipAmount: Varies by scholarship, examples include up to $13,500 for the National Buckeye Scholarship and full cost of attendance for the Stamps Eminence Scholarship. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: Ohio State's holistic review for the Columbus campus considers academic achievement, rigor of curriculum, ACT/SAT scores (required for 2026), and personal achievements.
Description: Studying history creates comprehension of complexity and diversity. This is an essential skill for negotiating today's multicultural, globalized world. A history major provides students with other skills too: the ability to write clearly and persuasively and to understand complicated events in a nuanced, sophisticated way. History majors learn to read newspapers, political speeches and documents in a critical fashion, a particularly vital skill in today's information-rich world.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management
Department: College of Education and Human Ecology

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Development and Family Science
Requirements: Upon admission to the university, students enroll directly into the human development and family science program as a pre-major. After completion of the following major admission requirements, students are placed in the major: complete 15 semester hours at Ohio State; earn at least a 2.0 cumulative GPA; complete economics and statistics with a grade of C- or higher. [13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Nutrition
Department: College of Education and Human Ecology
Concentration: ['Dietetics', 'Nutrition sciences', 'Nutrition in industry']
Description: Human nutrition is an integrated discipline focused on the role of diet in the prevention and treatment of disease. The human nutrition program is committed to the discovery of new information about the relationships between diet, physical activity, health and disease, and the application of such knowledge to individuals, communities and entire populations. All students in human nutrition complete course work in the fundamentals of human nutrition, food in different cultures, nutrition education, nutrition across the life cycle, issues and controversies in nutrition, advanced human nutrition, and nutrition careers as well as foundational courses in anatomy, biochemistry, biology, chemistry, microbiology and physiology.
Accredidation: The Ohio State University’s Didactic Program in Dietetics is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics 120 South Riverside Plaza, Suite 2190, Chicago, IL 60606-6995, (312) 899-0040 ext 5400, acend@eatright.org. https://www.eatrightpro.org/acend. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Industrial and Systems Engineering
Requirements: To apply to the Bachelor of Science in Industrial and Systems Engineering program at The Ohio State University, prospective students must first be admitted to the university. The application process is for general admission to the university, not directly to the major. Admission to a major in the College of Engineering happens after a student has completed their first year and has met the specific criteria for the major, which typically includes performance in foundational engineering and math courses. For first-year applicants to the university, a completed application, official high school transcripts, and a school report are required. ACT/SAT scores are optional for the 2026 application cycle. Admitted students who express interest in engineering are initially enrolled in the pre-major program within the College of Engineering.
Concentration: ['Data Analytics and Optimization', 'Supply Chain Management and Logistics', 'Management Systems and Operations Research', 'Manufacturing', 'Human Systems Integration and Design']
Description: Students in the industrial and systems engineering program gain a strong engineering foundation coupled with core course work in engineering economics, simulation, optimization, quality control, supply chain management and logistics, project management, manufacturing processes, workplace and facility design, ergonomics, lean engineering, systems thinking and cognitive systems engineering. In addition to the college core and major courses, engineering students also take select core courses and general education courses. Graduates of the industrial systems engineering program develop strong technical, management and design skills that are valuable to many different industries. They pursue a variety of career paths, including jobs in manufacturing and production, health care, finance, energy systems, retail and distribution, aviation, information technology, marketing, and education.
Accredidation: The Industrial and Systems Engineering (B.S.) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and Program Criteria for Industrial Engineering and Systems Engineering and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Studies
Requirements: Ohio State has a test-optional policy for 2026 applicants. Admission is competitive, and the university completes a holistic review of each student's application. The following factors are considered: performance in high school (class rank and GPA), the rigor of the high school curriculum, an application essay, and any submitted ACT or SAT scores.
Concentration: ['African Studies', 'Development Studies', 'East Asian Studies', 'Globalization Studies', 'Human Rights', 'Information Security', 'International Conflict & Peace', 'International Relations and Diplomacy', 'Latin American Studies', 'Middle East Studies', 'Security and Intelligence', 'Slavic and East European Studies', 'Western European Studies', 'World Business and Economy']
Description: The undergraduate international studies program provides internationally focused, cross-cultural course work at Ohio State. In cooperation with departments in several colleges, it offers undergraduates interdisciplinary major and minor programs of study concerning different world regions as well as contemporary global themes. The program is housed in the College of Arts and Sciences.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Journalism
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the journalism major, students must first be enrolled at Ohio State as pre-journalism majors. They must then complete two pre-major courses, COMM 1100 and COMM 1101, with a grade of C- or better in both. [8] Admission to the major is competitive and is based on cumulative grade point average, the completion of pre-major courses, and enrollment capacity. [4, 8] Students are required to complete a brief online application to be considered for the major. [4]
Concentration: Photojournalism and Documentary Photography
Description: Public Affairs Journalism (PAJ) teaches you how to investigate and disseminate news. [15] Our multimedia focus prepares you to integrate this training with the multimedia skills necessary for packaging news stories with word, still photo, audio and video. [15] As a journalism student, you also are taught to consider the context in which you will practice the field, including an understanding of the social, legal, and ethical implications that all journalists encounter. [15] Our students focus on reporting, interviewing, news writing and feature writing, as well as more interactive journalism such as blogging, micro blogging, social media and multimedia. [15] To better allow for domain-specific expertise, students in our journalism program complete a minor in an approved area-such as political science, international studies, business, criminology, etc.--that best fits their interests. [15] All journalism students further hone their "real-world" skills by working on our pride-and-joy publication, The Lantern, named Ohio's Best College Newspaper, as well as by participating in a journalism-related internship. [15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Landscape Architecture
Requirements: No prior experience or portfolio is required to apply. First-year students who begin at Ohio State as landscape architecture majors are eligible to continue into the second year upon earning a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or above and earning a B+ or higher in both architecture foundation courses. [12]
Description: Students in the landscape architecture program in the Knowlton School combine critical thinking skills with artistic principles, environmental consciousness and construction technology to address people's relationship to the land in a range of situations. [4, 14] They develop practical and evolving knowledge and skills as the foundation for professional competence, academic scholarship and individualized enrichment. [4, 14] The landscape architecture curriculum is structured around studio—an intense one-on-one pedagogy modeled after a traditional apprenticeship—supported by lectures, seminars and courses in technology, ecology, digital representation and history/theory. [4] Projects range from the design of small gardens to regional agricultural and ecosystems planning. [4] During the first year, students gain a foundation in design and an awareness of the built environment. [4] Through a process of drawing and making models, students learn to develop and communicate ideas across landscape architecture, architecture and urban design. [4]
Accredidation: Ohio State's Bachelor of Science in Landscape Architecture (BSLA) is a four-year accredited professional degree leading to licensure. [4, 14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics
Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language. The undergraduate program in linguistics at Ohio State will introduce you to the systematic study of the structure of human language and to the methods used to describe and analyze a variety of languages and dialects. All students gain a solid foundation in the core areas of linguistics: phonetics (the study of speech sounds), phonology (the study of sound patterns), syntax (the study of sentence structure), and semantics (the study of meaning). In addition, students have the opportunity to take a number of elective courses that allow them to explore the relationship between linguistics and a variety of other disciplines. Topics covered in the elective courses include the study of language and the brain, computational linguistics, language and culture, child language acquisition, the historical development of languages, and language variation and change.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: For admission to The Ohio State University as a first-year student, applicants must be a high school graduate or have earned a GED. The application process is for individuals who have not enrolled at a college or university after high school graduation, excluding college courses taken during high school. [4, 8] The university considers various factors for admission, including academic performance. [4]
Concentration: ['biomaterials', 'ceramics', 'electronic materials', 'metallurgy', 'polymers', 'manufacturing']
Description: An interdisciplinary field, materials science and engineering (MSE) studies materials from a variety of perspectives—their atomic and molecular structure, their properties, their processing and their performance in applications. Materials scientists and engineers are essential to every engineering discipline. They are on the forefront of technology, and they enable all other engineering fields by designing new materials for new applications, by developing materials that are more sustainable and by finding ways to make materials more affordably. Students in MSE may focus on ceramics, metallurgy, biomaterials, polymers, electronic materials and manufacturing. [8]
Accredidation: The Materials Science and Engineering program (B.S.) is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Materials, Metallurgical, Ceramics and similarly named Engineering Programs Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics
Concentration: ['Applied Math (Physics or Chemistry track)', 'Biology', 'Education', 'Financial Math', 'Honors', 'Theoretical']
Description: The Ohio State University Department of Mathematics offers students tools for understanding our world and trying to solve its problems. More than ever, mathematicians have an opportunity to make a lasting contribution to society by helping to solve problems in such diverse fields as medicine, management, economics, government, computer science, physics, psychology, engineering and social science. [3] The mathematics program at Ohio State provides students with the analytical and logical training necessary for diverse professions. [9] The formal requirements for the mathematics major are very flexible, allowing students to take courses in areas such as biological and physical sciences, management, finance, linguistics, social sciences, statistics, and computer and engineering sciences. [9] Mathematics majors are also encouraged to double major or complete a minor in other departments to apply their mathematical skills. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
Requirements: Admission to Ohio State is competitive. The university's admissions process considers a student's academic record, including the difficulty of their high school curriculum and their performance in it. While there are no specific additional requirements mentioned for the Bachelor of Science in Mathematics program itself beyond the general university admission requirements, students are expected to have a strong academic background.
Concentration: ['Theoretical Mathematics Track', 'Applied Mathematics Track (Physics or Chemistry options)', 'Biological Mathematics Track', 'Mathematics for Educators Track', 'Financial Mathematics Track', 'Honors Mathematics Track']
Description: The mathematics major introduces students to the areas of real and complex analysis, number theory, abstract algebra, logic and other fields. [6] A bachelor's degree in mathematics is designed to provide students with the analytical and logical training necessary for many diverse professions. [6] These students find that their skills in quantitative reasoning are in demand in many careers and are needed for many different positions, very few of which have mathematics in the job title. [6] Mathematics study can be designed to support different career goals, such as employment in business and industry, biology and medicine, development of new products using physics and chemistry, preprofessional education, or preparation for graduate school. [6]
Accredidation: The Ohio State University-Main Campus is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission; specific accreditation for the Bachelor of Science in Mathematics program is not mentioned. [18]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for the Mechanical Engineering major, freshmen applying to the Columbus campus are strongly encouraged to submit their complete admission application by November 1. Admitted first-year students begin in a pre-major program and complete prerequisite coursework before applying to the major. The Office of Undergraduate Admissions reviews applicants holistically. [6]
Concentration: ['Aerospace Engineering', 'Advanced Manufacturing']
Description: The bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering offers a curriculum that combines classroom learning with engineering practice. A broad spectrum of coursework is available for learning the fundamentals of engineering science, analysis, and design. State-of-the-art labs provide unmatched, hands-on experience to students through design and research projects.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Science
Requirements: Admission to the Medical Laboratory Science program is based on a holistic review of each candidate, including academic achievement in prerequisites and the student's overall cumulative grade-point average. Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 2.50 to be considered for admission. [12] Applicants are required to complete all prerequisite courses with a C- or higher prior to beginning professional course work. [12] Admission considerations include overall academic achievement (cumulative GPA), strong academic performance in math, chemistry, and biology (science GPA), knowledge of the field with a strong personal statement, and completion of program prerequisites. [12]
Department: School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences
Concentration: ['Certification Track', 'Medical Science Track', 'MLT Articulation Track', 'Coordinated Graduate Track']
Description: The Medical Laboratory Science program provides students with an undergraduate education in clinical laboratory science and prepares graduates to become certified medical laboratory scientists (MLS) and/or pursue post-baccalaureate studies in medical, dental, optometry or other graduate or professional program. [14] Medical laboratory science is the use of clinical laboratory tests to detect, diagnose, monitor and treat disease. [15] Blood, tissue and body fluids can be chemically analyzed and examined for foreign organisms and abnormalities. [15] Medical laboratory scientists are laboratory professionals who are part of the medical team of specialists that works together to determine the presence, extent or absence of disease. [15] They perform a full range of laboratory tests, from simple blood screens to more complex tests to detect diseases like cancer, coronary artery disease and diabetes. [15] They analyze, evaluate and validate laboratory data in the five major areas of the clinical laboratory: chemistry, immunology, hematology, transfusion medicine and microbiology. [15, 16] This information is then used by the medical team to make decisions regarding a patient's medical care. [15] Greater than 70% of all medical decisions are based on the results of clinical laboratory testing. [15, 16]
Accredidation: The Medical Laboratory Science program at The Ohio State University is accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences (NAACLS).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Music
Requirements: Academic admission to the university is a separate process from the School of Music application and audition. All prospective music majors must apply to both the university and, if they wish to take instrumental or vocal lessons, to the School of Music through the Acceptd® platform. An audition is required for the Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Music degree only if the student desires to take lessons as part of the program. Students who plan to pursue the BA degree but do NOT want to take lessons are not required to audition or submit a separate music application, but should complete an interest form. [3, 4, 5, 12]
Department: School of Music, College of Arts and Sciences
Fees: For the 2025-2026 academic year, undergraduate tuition and fees were set by cohort. In addition to general tuition, there is a Music program fee of $162 per semester. [27]
Concentration: ['Performance', 'Musicology', 'Theory/Composition', 'Jazz Studies', 'Open Music Electives']
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Music is the liberal arts degree program of choice for many of our students who wish to combine scholarly studies spanning a broad range of courses with music, or to pursue a major that can combine readily with a second major program in another field. [3] Scholarly course work is central to the BA degree. [3] Students in this program participate in ensembles, have the opportunity for private study (with audition) in voice or a primary instrument, and participate fully in the School of Music. [3] Graduates of the BA program may wish to pursue graduate work in a variety of music disciplines. [3] In addition, the BA in music can be a foundation for work in many other arts-related areas, including arts administration, music publishing, journalism and music therapy. [3] Students with special interests in music theory or musicology can take additional coursework in these areas as electives. [3]
CostPerCredit: For the Autumn 2024 and Spring 2025 terms, the per-credit-hour instructional fee for part-time students (1-11 credit hours) on the Columbus campus was $507.50 for residents. [27]
ScholarshipType: The School of Music offers talent-based scholarships, an Undergraduate Scholarship Assistance Fund, and small cash grants like The Brahms Fund. [26, 35] The university also offers merit-based scholarships. [26]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music Composition
Description: TThe Bachelor of Music in Composition offers students an excellent, comprehensive undergraduate curriculum in music composition. Our pedagogy centers around developing an understanding and control of the craft of composing by studying and applying both historical and current compositional trends and techniques through extensive listening, discussion, debate and diligent work. [13] At Ohio State, the programs of study in composition are truly multi-faceted. For decades our goal has been to offer students a wide range of options in diverse areas of concentration supported by an active faculty whose interests are both varied and comprehensive. [13] This strategy has successfully prepared our students for present-day careers that require not only specialized expertise but also the broad background needed to capitalize on opportunities. [13] We are committed to advocacy for our students and their careers. Our students are active in promoting their music locally, regionally, nationally and internationally, winning competitions and grants and having their music performed at national and international venues. [13] Coursework in Composition includes applied composition lessons and related courses including composition studio class, composers' workshop, counterpoint, orchestration, electronic music, and special-topics courses such as spectral music and film scoring. [13]
Accredidation: The Ohio State University is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [15]
CostPerCredit: The per-credit-hour rate for an Ohio resident undergraduate at the Columbus campus (for those taking 1-11 credit hours) is composed of a $507.50 instructional fee and a $22.83 general fee, totaling $530.33 per credit hour based on 2024-2025 rates. [18, 19]
ScholarshipType: The Ohio State University offers various types of scholarships to first-year students, which include merit-based scholarships awarded for academic achievement and restricted scholarships that consider additional criteria such as financial need or a specific field of interest.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music Performance
Concentration: ['Instrumental', 'Keyboard', 'Voice']
Description: The music performance degree at Ohio State focuses on the mastery of performance skills. We offer three tracks within the degree: instrumental, keyboard and voice. Our students benefit from professors who maintain active performance careers, and from opportunities available in Columbus' thriving arts community. [9] At Ohio State, students majoring in a brass, woodwind, percussion or string instrument are guided through a rigorous course of study in technique, performance practice, pedagogy and repertoire development by our artist faculty. [9] In addition to the required curricular studies, there are a number of elective courses available, such as the health-focused Alexander Technique class and a performance enhancement course. [9]
CostPerCredit: For the Autumn 2024-Spring 2025 academic year, the per-credit-hour instructional fee for undergraduate students taking between 1-11 credit hours was $507.50. This does not include other mandatory fees.
ScholarshipType: The Ohio State University offers a variety of scholarships, which generally fall into categories such as merit-based, need-based, and for the School of Music, talent or performance-based.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music Education in Music Education
Bachelor of Science in Nursing
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) program at The Ohio State University College of Nursing is a four-year, on-campus program that prepares students to become licensed registered nurses. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the sciences, humanities and nursing theory, with clinical experiences in a variety of settings. Students will learn to provide patient-centered care, work in interprofessional teams, and use evidence-based practice to improve patient outcomes.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing program at The Ohio State University is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences
Concentration: ['Drug discovery and development', 'Patient care']
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences (BSPS) program provides exceptional training for success in a variety of health care or research-oriented/non-clinical graduate programs and careers. The program's innovative coursework emphasizes cutting-edge integrated science learning, hands-on laboratory experiences and career development.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy
Description: The philosophy major trains students in rigorous, analytical reasoning and teaches them to solve problems and communicate logically and persuasively, both in speech and in writing. By studying classic texts and contemporary problems, students learn how to construct powerful arguments while pondering some of the deepest questions in human life: What makes for a meaningful life? Do humans have free will? What is the nature of consciousness and can it be explained? Is the existence of a benevolent and all-powerful God compatible with the existence of natural and human evil? What is the nature of right and wrong? Are there objective moral standards? Students in the philosophy program learn how to explore answers to these fundamental questions by debating and defending complex ideas and arguments and expressing beliefs with clarity and precision. They develop a sensitivity to the assumptions that underlie our factual and evaluative judgments, and become careful and critical readers, writers, listeners and thinkers.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Physics
Bachelor of Science in Physics
Concentration: ['Applied Physics Option', 'Advanced Physics Option', 'Advanced Physics Option (Honors)', 'Physics and Life Sciences Option', 'Teaching Option']
Description: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Physics from the College of Arts & Sciences is designed to allow flexibility for students interested in physics and to prepare them for a wide variety of career paths. [2] For students enrolled at OSU prior to autumn 2024, there are four different options/tracks to choose from based on their post-graduation and career plans: the Applied Physics Option for students planning to work full-time after graduation or continue their education in other fields; the Advanced Physics Option (including an Honors version) for those planning to earn a Ph.D. in Physics; the Physics and Life Sciences Option for Pre-Health students; and the Teaching Option for students interested in teaching high school physics. [2, 8] All options lead to a Bachelor of Science in Physics. [8] The program provides training for various careers, including employment as a scientist, engineer, or teacher; pursuit of a graduate degree in Physics, Astronomy, or Math; and careers in other areas like Medicine, Law, or Business. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Concentration: ['Democracy and law', 'Political identities and allegiances', 'Political economy and development', 'Cooperation, conflict and violence', 'Inequality and justice', 'Political leadership and reform', 'Political analysis', 'American Politics']
Description: The BA degree program offers Political Science students a wide range of opportunities to study the many dimensions of politics and government including elections and electoral behavior, legal and judicial politics, foreign policy and war, political economy and development, the political implications of race, gender and ethnicity, and the moral and ethical issues associated with democracy, global justice, and human rights.
Accredidation: The Ohio State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Psychology
Fees: For the 2025-2026 academic year, undergraduate tuition and fees for the Columbus campus were not yet published with a specific total. However, for the 2024-2025 academic year, which is the most recent available information, the estimated total for an in-state student was $13,244 and for an out-of-state student was $40,022. There is also a specific program fee for Psychology students of $104.40 per semester for a full-time student. [10, 18, 32]
Description: Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. Psychology majors at Ohio State receive broad training in the current methods and content of the discipline. Students who study psychology at Ohio State take courses in the brain and behavior, cognitive psychology, developmental psychology, abnormal psychology and social psychology. Psychology students have access to faculty who are prominent researchers and have opportunities to work alongside them in research labs.
CostPerCredit: For the 2024-2025 academic year, the per-credit-hour instructional fee for undergraduate students at the Columbus Campus (for those taking 1-11 credit hours) is $507.50. Additional fees also apply. [32]
ScholarshipAmount: The university offers several full cost of attendance scholarships, such as the Stamps Eminence Scholarship and the President's Ohio Scholarship Program. [9]
ScholarshipType: The university offers a variety of scholarships, including merit-based scholarships, need-based aid such as the Land Grant Opportunity Scholarship, and program-specific scholarships like the Choose Ohio First scholarship for STEM fields. [4, 9, 14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
Description: The Bachelor of Science in psychology focuses on the biological and neuroscientific aspects of psychology, which are increasingly important in research and clinical practice. You'll also study topics including neuroscience, memory, personality and cognition while building a strong foundation in scientific principles. The coursework combines theoretical learning with hands-on experiences, allowing you to apply your knowledge to real-world situations. The curriculum consists of 36 credit hours of psychology courses and a prerequisite course, Introduction to Psychology. Course work for the psychology major includes: Data Analysis in Psychology, Research Methods in Psychology, and a core course from each of four areas: brain and behavior, cognitive psychology, clinical and development psychology, and social psychology. [6, 7] In addition, students completing a BS degree must also take Quantitative and Statistical Methods in Psychology, and an advanced research course. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Health
Bachelor of Science in Public Health in Environmental Public Health
Concentration: Environmental Public Health
Description: The environmental public health specialization is for students who have an interest in both the environment and health, how environments impact health and a desire to find solutions to the challenges of environmental effects on the health of communities. The curriculum provides students with an interdisciplinary education in public health and environmental science. [3] This program provides a broad pre-professional foundation covering basic and applied science and math relative to sources of contaminants from air, water, soil, food and the related aspects of human exposure and impact. [6]
Accredidation: The BSPH major has a competency-based curriculum that aligns with criteria from the Council on Education in Public Health (CEPH). [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Public Health in Public Health Sociology
Concentration: Public Health Sociology
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Public Health (BSPH) degree offers two interdisciplinary specializations: environmental public health and public health sociology. The public health sociology specialization blends courses from the Department of Sociology in the College of Arts and Sciences with public health courses. [3] This program provides a broad pre-professional foundation by expanding shared and complimentary principles of sociology and public health relative to population health and intervention. [3] The public health sociology specialization teaches how social factors impact health in order to improve the health of communities. [5] The curriculum blends select courses from sociology with public health providing a unique interdisciplinary education. [5]
Accredidation: The BSPH major has a competency-based curriculum that aligns with criteria from the Council on Education in Public Health (CEPH). [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Radiologic Sciences and Therapy
Concentration: ['Echocardiography', 'Radiation Therapy', 'Radiography', 'Diagnostic Medical Sonography']
Description: Radiologic sciences and therapy professionals are the collective health professions that use imaging (X-ray, CT, MRI, mammography, Interventional radiography, linear accelerators and ultrasound) for medical diagnosis, assessment and treatment of disease. [3] The radiologic sciences and therapy major at Ohio State offers three distinct degree tracks: radiography, which provides diagnostic tests through X-Rays, CT scans and MRIs; diagnostic medical sonography, which is more commonly known as 'ultrasound technology'; and radiation therapy, which is used to treat disease with concentrated beams of radiation. [3] Ohio State's Radiologic Sciences and Therapy Program was designed to train those professionals needed in the healthcare industry. [2] Our bachelor's degree program is unlike other training as it combines freshman and sophomore general courses with the specializations and clinical practice that makes our graduates more marketable. [2] Students in this major are part of a cohort that take courses together and receive individualized attention from faculty. [3] Students begin the major with extensive theory and clinical education in the use of radiation (ionizing and nonionizing) for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. [3] Additional instruction and clinical education is provided in adjunct areas to complete the radiologic science professionals' education. [3]
Accredidation: For the past five years, 100% of students have passed the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists registry exam (10–14 percentage points higher than the national average). [3] The program is accredited by the Joint Review Committee on Education in Radiologic Technology. [13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Respiratory Therapy
Concentration: ['Neonatal and pediatric care', 'Rehabilitation and continuing care', 'Education', 'Administration', 'Noninvasive cardiac diagnostic testing', 'Hyperbaric oxygen', 'Sleep disorders', 'Pulmonary function laboratories']
Description: Respiratory therapists are licensed healthcare professionals who provide testing, treatment and care to patients who have difficulty breathing. Graduates are trained to work with the full spectrum of patients, from infants to older adults. Therapists work in many different settings, including intensive care units, emergency departments, diagnostic laboratories, clinics and the home. Admitted first-year students begin in pre-respiratory therapy. There they complete the prerequisite course work necessary to apply to the respiratory therapy major. The professional course work begins in the junior year and consists of five consecutive terms of enrollment, which includes one summer term, comprised of over 60 credit hours in respiratory therapy and professional supporting courses. The major also affords students opportunities to select clinical specialties. [10, 13]
Accredidation: The Respiratory Therapy baccalaureate program at The Ohio State University, Columbus, Ohio has continued accreditation from the Commission on Accreditation for Respiratory Care (CoARC). Our program number is 200167. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology
Description: Sociology is the study of group life. Because human behavior is diverse, the field of sociology covers a diversity of subjects. Sociologists may specialize in the family, the urban community, education, health and medicine, social movements, deviance, crime and law, religion, politics, work and occupations, sports and leisure, race and ethnic minorities, gender and sex roles, or other areas of human behavior. [11] A sociology degree at Ohio State provides students with the scientific skills and social perspective necessary to analyze and understand the complexities of modern societies and to address challenging social problems. [14] Sociology is a liberal arts/social science major that provides graduates with the scientific tools and the perspective necessary to better understand social issues and complex societal problems. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Social Work
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Social Work Program at The Ohio State University prepares leaders in generalist social work practice through rigorous academic and field education grounded in the core values and ethics of the profession. [4] Graduates are evidence-informed practitioners who apply a person-in-environment framework to promote the health and well-being of individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities. [4] The BSSW curriculum, which includes field practice (internship) experiences, prepares students to become highly competent social workers who advance human rights, engage in practice-informed research and policy practice, and effectively encounter and strategically work with individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities. [5] Students learn skills in client engagement, assessment, service planning, case management, crisis intervention, program evaluation, community organizing and advocacy. [14] While there are no formal concentrations, the online BSSW program offers electives in areas such as trauma, forensic social work, crisis intervention, suicidology, and social work with military and veteran populations. [5]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Social Work (BSSW) and the Master of Social Work (MSW) programs are accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE). Both programs were reaffirmed for accreditation until October 2026. [3] The Ohio State University's College of Social Work is the oldest continuously accredited public social work program in the country. [4, 19]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Spanish
Concentration: ['Track in Iberian Literatures and Cultures', 'Track in Latin American Literatures and Cultures', 'Track in Hispanic Linguistics', 'Track in Hispanic Studies']
Description: The Spanish major consists of a minimum of 33 credit hours distributed as indicated below. A minimum grade of "C-" in all courses counting toward the major is required. Honors students must take 3450H and fulfill additional requirements. (H) and (E) denotes Honors and Embedded Honors versions available. Non-Honors students must meet minimum GPA and pre-requisite requirements to be considered for enrollment in Honors or Embedded Honors sections.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Special Education
Concentration: ['Dual Licensure Primary General Education & Intervention Specialist (P-5)', 'Mild to Intensive Dual Licensure Intervention Specialist (K-12)']
Description: The undergraduate special education program is a competitive major that will prepare you to meet the educational needs of diverse learners with disabilities. Specifically, this program will prepare you with the skills to earn an intervention specialist license to teach children who have learning, behavior, or developmental disabilities in a variety of settings and across a wide range of ages/grades. [5]
Accredidation: Ohio State educator preparation programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) through 2026. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Speech and Hearing Science
Description: The aachelor of rts () degree in peech and earing cience rovides students foundational knowledge in the study of normal and disordered functioning of the auditory system, the speech mechanism, and language processing. e repare students to think critically about how eople communicate with one another and experience the world around them. tudents are introduced to both basic and applied research and to clinical applications. peech and earing cience is a diverse field which draws upon a number of other disciplines, including anatomy, physiology, psychology, linguistics, physics, engineering, medicine, and education. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sport Industry
Description: Ohio State's sport industry major prepares you to thrive within the vibrant, diverse, and compelling world of sports. The program provides the academic preparation and training to undertake research on issues pertaining to the sport industry and to succeed at the graduate level in sports management, sport studies, and related fields. Students receive a complete academic experience maintained through excellence in teaching, research, and community engagement. The curriculum is designed to develop the skills to compete and thrive in the sport industry, including skills related to programming, management, leadership, promotion, marketing, law, and communication. Students will be instilled with the social, cultural, historical, and ethical contexts to serve as responsible stewards of their chosen professions. The program prepares students for supervisory, leadership, and administrative positions in the sport and leisure industry and/or for graduate programs in sport humanities, sport management, and sport law. It combines social science and humanities disciplines to provide students with the needed theory and practice for entrance into the sport and leisure industry, informing them of the constantly changing themes, issues, and practices the industry confronts. Students will comprehend the social, economic, political, and legal issues that shape the development of the industry. [5, 6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theatre
Concentration: ['acting', 'new works development', 'design', 'technical theatre']
Description: The Department of Theatre, Film, and Media Arts at Ohio State is committed to a liberal arts approach to theatre education. The Bachelor of Arts degree prepares students to become self-reliant theatre makers with a rich understanding of the role of performance in public culture. [3] Through a liberal arts curriculum, the theatre program at Ohio State prepares students as self-reliant theatre makers with rich understandings of the role of performance in contemporary society. [14] The Theatre Major is a flexible BA degree with required coursework in five main categories: history and text, design, performance, production, and experiential learning. [14] Students can customize their program of study to focus on acting, new works development, design, or technical theatre through major electives. [14]
Accredidation: The Department of Theatre, Film, and Media Arts is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST). [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Vision Science
Description: The BSVS is for highly motivated, well qualified a student's education who wants to fast-track their Optometry education. Students pursuing this option would be able to complete both a Bachelor of Science degree and a Doctor of Optometry (OD) degree in a total of seven years, reducing both the time to career entry and total cost of education by one year. Candidates would complete the General Education Requirements for a Bachelor of Science and the OD prerequisites in the first three years of their undergraduate career. Then, if admitted to the Ohio State College of Optometry, the courses taken in the first year of the OD program would be applied to the BSVS and the degree would be awarded in the spring of that year, thus allowing students to graduate with their undergraduate cohort. Students would then complete the remaining three years of the OD program.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Women's, Gender and Sexuality Studies
Description: The Department of Women's, Gender and Sexuality Studies (WGSS) at Ohio State is one of the nation's top WGSS programs. The WGSS major is an interdisciplinary program that examines how systems of oppression, resistance and privilege operate. It is designed to provide students with an understanding of the importance of gender and sexuality as categories of analysis and their intersections with race, ethnicity, class, age, nationality and (dis)ability. [9]

ProgramName: Associate of Arts in General Studies
Concentration: general studies
Description: The Associate of Arts Degree at The Ohio State University at Lima is a two-year liberal arts degree that gets students started on an exciting relationship with learning that will last a lifetime. In two short years, students can receive an Ohio State degree and the pride and opportunities that come with being a Buckeye. This program is designed for students who are interested in additional教育after an exciting relationship with learning that will last a lifetime. This program is designed for students who are interested in a solid educational foundation but aren't sure of all their options. Others may be undecided about a major but would still like to start college. Students in this program take coursework that will count toward all majors or degree programs so when they finally decide on a career path, they have already fulfilled much of the required coursework. This is not a terminal degree like some technical-based associate's degrees; all of the credits apply directly toward a baccalaureate degree at Ohio State.

ProgramName: Associate of Applied Science in Agricultural Commerce
Concentration: Agricultural Business
Description: The Associate of Applied Science in Business Management at Ohio State ATI provides students with knowledge and skills in key business areas including accounting, marketing and sales, business finance, and management. This program aims to equip students with the necessary tools to start, run, and manage a business successfully. The Agricultural Business specialization allows students to select a specialty in agriculture and take a minimum of six credit hours within that chosen area. [12]
Accredidation: Ohio State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). In June 2015, the Board of the HLC voted to consolidate the separate accreditations of Ohio State University and Ohio State University Agricultural Technical Institute into a single accreditation under the University. [16]

ProgramName: Associate of Applied Science in Agriscience Education
Concentration: agricultural science/production specialization
Description: Agriscience education is one of 29 career-focused associate degree and certificate programs offered at Ohio State's Agricultural Technical Institute (ATI) in Wooster. [3] The Agriscience Education program is designed to prepare students for teaching careers in the public schools, extension agencies/offices, or in agricultural businesses or organizations. [4] The Associate of Science degree program at Ohio State ATI allows students to complete 50 percent of the curriculum needed to complete a Bachelor of Science degree in Agriscience Education at The Ohio State University in Columbus. [4] The curriculum of the Agriscience Education program will focus on the agricultural science/production specialization. [4]
Accredidation: Ohio State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). [5]

ProgramName: Associate of Applied Science in Business Management
Associate of Applied Science in Construction Management
Associate of Applied Science in Culinary Science
Associate of Applied Science in Dental Hygiene
Associate of Applied Science in Early Childhood Education
Associate of Applied Science in Engineering Technology
Description: The Associate of Applied Science in Engineering Technology prepares students for technician-level positions in all branches of the engineering profession. The program stresses application of scientific and engineering principles through laboratory experiences. The engineering technology curriculum includes a strong background in communications, mathematics and science. Graduates will be prepared to assist engineers in the areas of product development, manufacturing, testing, and service. This program provides an excellent background for a number of bachelor’s degree programs in engineering technology.

ProgramName: Associate of Applied Science in Radiologic Technology
Associate of Science
Concentration: Agricultural Systems Management, with specialization areas in Agribusiness and Agronomy.
Description: The Agricultural Systems Management (ASM) program at Ohio State ATI is a hands-on associate degree that equips students with the practical skills and technical knowledge needed to succeed in modern farming and agribusiness. Students learn to solve real-world problems in agricultural operations by blending coursework in machinery systems, construction, electronics, and resource management, with a strong emphasis on applied learning. The program is designed to transfer seamlessly into a Bachelor of Science degree at The Ohio State University and prepares students for a variety of roles in the agricultural industry. Students gain experience in areas such as machinery operation and performance, soil and water conservation, welding and fabrication, building systems, and agricultural electronics. A required ten-week internship allows students to apply their skills in a real-world setting and build professional connections.

ProgramName: Minor in Accounting
Description: The Accounting minor is designed to provide undergraduate business students and others not majoring in Accounting the opportunity to gain exposure to and build competence in Accounting. [6]

ProgramName: Minor in Agribusiness
Description: Students will understand: (1) the business concepts important for effective agribusiness decision-making and management, and (2) the role of economic constraints in the efficient operation of an agribusiness firm. Emphasis is placed on applying concepts and skills to the food system. Firms in the food system may include agro-chemical companies, bio-engineering firms, farms, agricultural cooperatives, international commodity trading firms, and international food distribution and retailing companies. [3, 6] The Agribusiness minor provides an understanding of business concepts important for effective agribusiness decision-making and an understanding of the role of economic constraints in the efficient operation of an agribusiness firm. [8]

ProgramName: Minor in Agricultural Communication
Description: The minor in Agricultural Communication is designed to provide students with basic knowledge and skills in communication related to agricultural and environmental sciences. [1, 8] Courses in the minor will develop oral and written communication skills and advance a student's use of electronic technologies to effectively communicate science-based information. [1, 8] This minor is designed for students interested in careers in technology transfer, marketing, government relations, public relations, sales, advertising, and non-profit organizations. [1, 8] The minor is open to students across the university interested in learning to effectively communicate science- based information to a variety of audiences. [1, 8]

ProgramName: Minor in Agricultural Systems Management
Description: The agricultural systems management minor is administered by the College of Food, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences. It is designed to provide students with an introduction to the physical systems and technology used in agriculture, food production and natural resources. (AGSYSMT-MN). [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Agronomy
Minor in Animal Sciences
Description: The animal science minor is administered by the College of Food, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences. This minor is for students who wish to develop an understanding about the principles of the beef, dairy, horse, poultry, sheep and swine industries. This minor will appeal to students with interests in animal production with an emphasis on genetics, nutrition and physiology. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Anthropology
Description: A minimum of 15 credit hours (5 courses) are required to minor in anthropology. The student may complete a minor by choosing the archaeology, cultural anthropology, physical anthropology, or forensic science track.

ProgramName: Minor in Arabic
Description: Arabic is a major and minor that prepare you to communicate effectively in one of the world's most influential languages while deepening your understanding of the people and cultures of the Arabic-speaking world. [4] Through progressive language study, you will build oral and written proficiency and explore the rich literary, cultural, and historical traditions of Arabic societies from the Arabian Peninsula across North Africa. [4] Whether your interests lie in language and linguistics, literature and media, international business and diplomacy, or global affairs, proficiency in Arabic opens doors to careers in education, government, international development, journalism, translation and interpretation, and more. [4] To complete the major, students take foundational language sequences, advanced language courses, literature and culture classes, and electives chosen with an academic advisor to reflect individual goals and interests. [4] The minor provides a concentrated path through key language and cultural courses that support both Arabic study and other fields. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Architecture
Description: Every engaged citizen will impact the physical environment, from renovating a family home to voting on large civic projects. Therefore, every student should be educated to make informed decisions when doing so. Through courses in this Minor, students arrive at an understanding insulators' world: a global ecology of diverse cultures linked by electronic media and the earth's limited resources. Because of architecture's broad cultural impact, the Minor in Architectural Studies is geared towards a wide audience. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Art
Concentration: ['Art and Technology', 'Ceramics', 'Film/Video', 'Glass', 'Painting and Drawing', 'Photography', 'Printmaking', 'Sculpture']
Description: The mission of the Department of Art is to inspire and enable people to lead creative and intellectually flexible lives. [10, 11] The Minor in Studio Art provides students with the opportunity to integrate creative and artistic practice with other academic or research pursuits. [4, 10, 11] The curriculum guides students through a range of class work that the Art faculty consider essential to understanding art making in both a material and conceptual sense. [4] This minor is designed for students who may not be pursuing careers as professional artists but are seeking to develop skills in visual arts and creativity, which are valuable in a wide range of disciplines and industries. [4, 10, 11] The program requires the completion of 15 semester credit hours, including foundation courses and electives from various areas of concentration. [10, 11]
Accredidation: The Department of Art at The Ohio State University is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD). [8]

ProgramName: Minor in Arts Entrepreneurship
Description: Trough the Arts Entrepreneurship minor, students will be able to develop entrepreneurial and managerial skills necessary to succeed as creative individuals in the increasingly complex economic environment of contemporary art-making. [3, 5] Students will attain business acumen and expertise necessary to operate arts and cultural institutions in the specific role of arts administrator. [5] They will exhibit the critical and creative skills needed by policy makers and the knowledge of varied cultural, social, and economic realities impacting contemporary art disciplines, creative sector collaborations, and the role of art in society. [3, 5]

ProgramName: Minor in Asian American Studies
Minor in Astronomy and Astrophysics
Description: The minor in astronomy and astrophysics consists of at least 12 credit hours of course work beyond the introductory calculus-based Physics courses (Physics 1250 and 1251, or equivalents), the introductory calculus courses (Math 1151 and 1152, or equivalents), and an introductory programming course (Astron 1221 or CSE 122x or equivalent). Courses at the 1000-level may not be counted towards completion of the minor program.

ProgramName: Minor in Athletic Coaching Education
Description: Learn how to effectively coach and administer youth and adolescent sports programs with this minor. You will learn theories and basics of coaching and organizing effective sports programs for schools, community agencies and other groups that need expertise with the administration of their sports programs. [8]

ProgramName: Minor in Aviation
Description: The Center for Aviation Studies in the College of Engineering gives students across campus a unique opportunity for exposure to the aviation field. The minor offers the experience of studying the real-world applications of aircraft design and other aspects of the aviation industry including finances, scheduling, operations, and airport planning. [4] Many students in aeronautical and astronautical engineering will minor in aviation to gain a hands-on understanding of the aircraft that they design. [6] If a student in any field wants to work in the aviation industry as a finance manager, scheduler, operations manager or airport planner, a minor in aviation is highly recommended. [3, 6] The minor in Aviation consists of a minimum of 15-17 credit hours of required and elective course work. [3, 4, 5]

ProgramName: Minor in Biochemistry
Minor in Bio-Scientific Illustration
Minor in Business
Description: The Business Minor is designed to provide students in majors other than business with an understanding of the language and basic concepts of business. The minor consists of five courses, one each from the areas of accounting, finance, management and human resources, marketing and operations management. This program is available to students on all Ohio State campuses.

ProgramName: Minor in Chemistry
Description: The minor in chemistry consists of a minimum of 17 credit hours of course work: Chemistry 2210 (5) and an additional 12 hours of chemistry courses above 2210, with a maximum of 10 credit hours of Chemistry 2310, 25xx, 26xx, and 29xxH. The minimum mathematics and physics courses required to support this program are Mathematics 1151 and Physics 1200 and 1201 or 1250 and 1251, but many chemistry courses at the 3000 level and above also require the completion of Mathematics 1152 (or higher as indicated). [3] Students with a special interest in chemistry or biochemistry may want to pursue a minor in one of these areas in addition to their chosen major. [10] Pre-Health students may choose a chemistry or biochemistry minor as a good complement to their major, strengthening their preparation for medical school, pharmacy, or other professional programs. [10] Business majors who want to pursue sales or marketing of chemicals or pharmaceuticals may choose a chemistry or biochemistry minor in order to strengthen their familiarity with chemical and biochemical terminology and concepts. [10]

ProgramName: Minor in Chinese
Description: The minor in Chinese consists of 15 credit hours of prerequisites and 14 credit hours of required course work. The purpose of the prerequisites is to give students the linguistic and cultural foundations upon which to build an understanding of China The courses beyond the prerequisites are intended to provide more substantial training in the Chinese language and further cultural understanding. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in City and Regional Planning
Description: The City and Regional Planning (CRP) Minor ensures that students will gain some exposure to history, theory or methods in city and regional planning. City and regional planning is a vibrant field that focuses on the future and quality of life in cities, towns, and regions. The curriculum is designed to be flexible to allow students to take courses that most meet their interests in city and regional planning.

ProgramName: Minor in Classics
Concentration: ['Greek Civilization', 'Roman Civilization']
Description: Students who wish to minor in Classics may choose between the Greek Civilization or Roman Civilization track. Courses in Greek and Roman literature and civilization are taught in translation. The Classics minor requires at least 4 courses (12 credit hours) to complete the minor, excluding prerequisites. [4] Students who have decided to declare their minor should meet with the Director of Undergraduate Studies or Academic Advisor to complete a Minor Program Form. This form lists all courses students will use to fulfill minor requirements and is one of the final contracts for graduation. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Communication
Description: The communication minor is designed to provide students with an understanding of the basic concepts of communication. There is one prerequisite course to the minor and the minor itself consists of four courses (12 credit hours). [7] The prerequisite course and the four courses in the minor cover each of the following areas: communication theory, communication technology, interpersonal communication, mass communication, and strategic communication. [7] The prerequisite course and all four courses in the minor must be completed to satisfy the minor requirements. [7]

ProgramName: Minor in Computer and Information Science
Concentration: ['Graphics', 'AI', 'Networking', 'Software Engineering', 'Databases', 'Programming languages', 'Theory']
Description: Students interested in applying computing principles and practices in another discipline (in which they may be completing a major degree program) should consider completing the Computer & Information Science (CIS) Minor program. The Computer and Information Science Minor is intended to permit students majoring in other disciplines to gain enough background and experience in computing foundations and software to understand in depth the relationships between their major field and computing. Graduates who can communicate in clear terms with software professionals who are tasked with designing computing applications (e.g., in the student's major field) are becoming increasingly valuable to employers. [9, 10]

ProgramName: Minor in Creative Writing
Minor in Criminology and Criminal Justice
Description: The Criminology and Criminal Justice Studies minor is designed to provide undergraduate students with focused knowledge of the nature and causes of juvenile and adult crime among individuals and across communities, the development and administration of criminal law with an emphasis on criminal procedure and capital punishment, the nature and functioning of criminal justice institutions including police, juvenile and adult criminal courts, and corrections. [2] The criminology minor provides students with a strong foundation to gain employment in any aspect of federal, state, and local criminal justice, security, law, public policy, social work, and business. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Dance
Minor in Design
Minor in Disability Studies
Description: Disability studies seeks to study the nature, meaning and consequences of disability in global culture from an integrated social, political, cultural model. [2] It incorporates historical, phenomenological, political, cultural, medical, sociological, technological, educational and legal perspectives in order to provide an enriched and coherent view of disability. [2, 4] The program treats disability as a political, cultural and social process, placing as much importance on structures, relations and representations as on individual bodies. [7] The minor is designed to provide a context for understanding the meaning and experience of difference in society by requiring students to examine how disability intersects with gender, race, class, age, & sexuality. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Earth Sciences
Concentration: ['Earth Sciences', 'Geoarchaeology', 'Mineralogy and Petrology', 'Economic Geology', 'Geochemistry', 'Paleontology', 'Environmental Studies', 'Geophysics']
Description: Students with majors in other areas may find that a minor in Earth Sciences provides sufficient background for employment in the geosciences or geoscience-related positions in the petroleum and mining industries, the environmental field, etc. The School of Earth Sciences offers eight subprograms in the Earth Sciences minor. Each minor program requires a coherent set of Earth Science courses and prerequisite courses. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in East Asian Languages and Literatures
Description: The minor in East Asian Languages and Literatures consists of 15 credit hours of prerequisites and 15 hours of course work beyond the prerequisites. The purpose of the prerequisites is to give students a fundamental language and cultural basis upon which to build an understanding of East Asia. The courses beyond the prerequisites are intended to provide substantial training in an East Asian language and further cultural understanding. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Economics
Description: Economics offers an understanding of how the economy operates and provides a basis for informed opinions on many public issues. An undergraduate minor in economics provides good preparation for careers in government, business, organized labor, trade associations, or teaching in the social sciences. It also provides an excellent base for graduate work in any of the social sciences or in professional schools such as law and business administration.

ProgramName: Minor in Education
Description: The education minor is designed to provide foundational knowledge about education within the larger social context and to offer a cross-disciplinary examination of the intersections of education, culture, and society. [4, 6] Students choosing to minor in education may wish to explore education as a possible career choice or they may be interested in studying current issues in the field as well as learning more about schools and schooling in today's society. [4, 14] The objectives for students are to: examine the legal, ethical, interpersonal and community issues that impact education across the life span of a learner; work closely with professionals and complete readings and tasks about current issues in education to explore a career as an educator; examine the relationships between education and the social, political, philosophical, and cultural contexts of the larger society; and study the hereditary and environmental factors that influence individuals' physical, cognitive, affective, social, and language development. [4, 6]

ProgramName: Minor in Engineering Sciences
Description:

This mirror is designed for non-engineering students with an interest in learning more about technology's important role in today's society; and who may be working with engineers and technology based opportunities in the future. [5] Specific learning goals include: • Develop a basic understanding of the engineering design process. [5] • Understand the capabilities and limitations of technologies and engineered systems. [5] • Be able to make informed decisions about engineering activities and technologies. [5] • Be able to work effectively as a member of a team including technology experts. [5] The program advisor will work with you on selection of a suitable minor program to meet your specific career objectives. [5] Upon completion of the minor, the advisor will approve and sign the Minor Program Form. [5] You may then file the Minor Program Form with your college or school to receive a minor in Engineering Sciences. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in English
Description: The English Minor at The Ohio State University prepares students to think critically about texts, construct sound arguments based on evidence, write elegantly and persuasively, and understand the historical and cultural contexts in which texts are produced, disseminated, and received. [3, 4] The program consists of a minimum of 12 total credit hours of English courses at the 2000 level or above. [3, 5] Students have access to over 120 courses on a wide range of topics including Shakespeare, digital media studies, popular culture, creative nonfiction, and film analysis. [5, 7]

ProgramName: Minor in Entomology
Minor in Entrepreneurship and Innovation
Description: The Undergraduate Entrepreneurship & Innovation Minor is offered through a collaboration of the following colleges: Fisher College of Business, the College of Engineering, and the College of Arts and Sciences (Department of Design). [10] Designed for capturing the economic value in creative ideas for commercially viable products and services, this educational program enhances a student's understanding of and appreciation for entrepreneurship and innovation. [10] The Entrepreneurship Minor is designed to empower students from any major to harness the economic value of innovative ideas. Through this program, students will strengthen their understanding of entrepreneurship and innovation, while exploring potential career paths and developing key competencies in launching, managing, and leading entrepreneurial ventures. [5] This minor is ideal for students interested in startups, social enterprises, innovation strategy, or launching their own business. [5] No application is required. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Environment, Economy, Development and Sustainability
Description: The minor in environment, economy, development and sustainability minor provides students with a multi-disciplinary approach to sustainability topics and problems with a focus on the economic, business and social change aspects of sustainability. [1] Pressing environmental issues such as climate change and water quality are fundamentally connected to human impacts and problems of resource scarcity, access and degradation. [1] Sustainability requires integrated approaches that can improve the well-being of society without causing irreparable harm to the Earth's ecological systems. [1] The EEDS minor offers students a multi-disciplinary program that focuses on the human, economic and environmental dimensions of sustainability – often referred to as people, planet and profit. [2] Through enrollment in the EEDS minor, students learn sustainability concepts to complement their work in their major program of study.
